settings.question: Do I legally have to mark my glass?
settings.answer: In workplaces, transparent doors and screens must be marked where it's needed for safety, under regulation 14 of the Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992. For building work, Approved Document K says where and at what height. We fit at those heights, but we can't certify your building. If you're unsure, ask your building control body or health and safety adviser.

settings.question: What heights do you use?
settings.answer: Two bands: 850–1000mm and 1400–1600mm above the floor, as set out in Approved Document K. Where the marking needs to stand out more, for example for people with poor sight, we can use a contrasting colour.

settings.question: Will frosting make the room dark?
settings.answer: No. Frosted vinyl lets light through and blocks the view. We can frost just a band at eye level so the room stays bright.

settings.question: Can it come off when we move?
settings.answer: Yes. It peels off cleanly, which suits rented offices. We can remove it for you too.

settings.question: Can you fit outside office hours?
settings.answer: Ask when you book. Most jobs take a few hours, and we fit around your working day where we can.

settings.question: Do you cover my area?
settings.answer: Fitting is free in HA4, HA5, HA6, UB8, UB9, UB10, HA1, HA2, HA3 and WD3. Further afield, ask us.
